hook: "From founders and creators to brand owners, everyone is building their personal brand through: Educational content…"
cta: none explicit — the question is the close ('So what's stopping you?').
idea: Educational content is one of the four personal-brand pillars — people want to know who you are before they buy or trust you.
sequencing: The trend: everyone builds personal brand.
The four pillars: educational, vlogs, entertaining, launch.
The challenge: so what's stopping you?
The reason: people want to know you before buying.
formatting: Motivational list post: the trend → the four pillars → the challenge. Link cut.
why_it_works: 'So what's stopping you?' turns observation into personal challenge. The know-before-buy line names the mechanism.
what_to_steal: The trust sequence (know you → buy from you) as LC's justification for founder/educational content: Jay teaching jewelry care builds the trust that converts.

hook: "Built a premium advertorial experience for @KYOM" — the 'premium advertorial' frame.
body: The showcase: a premium advertorial experience for @KYOM — emotional storytelling + educational content + social proof + conversion-focused design — turning a simple haircare product into a luxury brand experience. 44s video.
cta: none explicit — portfolio showcase (link to the work).
idea: A premium advertorial that fuses emotional storytelling, educational content, social proof, and conversion design to lift a simple haircare product into a luxury brand experience.
sequencing: The transformation: simple product → luxury experience.
formatting: Portfolio flex: one-line build description stacking four disciplines, 44s video.
why_it_works: Stacking four disciplines in one line makes the work sound comprehensive. 'Transform a simple product into luxury' names the alchemy every DTC brand wants.
what_to_steal: The 4-ingredient advertorial stack as LC's premium PDP/quiz template: story → education (materials) → proof (reviews) → conversion design. 'Simple product → luxury experience' is LC's exact positioning job.

hook: "Depends on the smm and the brand's persona" — the conditional frame.
cta: none explicit — the framework is the content.
idea: The complaint-response triage: witty response if the brand is witty and conditions are perfect; educational content if the bad experience came from misuse; always a sincere apology + solution.
sequencing: The conditional: depends on SMM + persona.
formatting: SMM triage framework: 3 response modes matched to conditions. Terse, practitioner.
why_it_works: Conditional frameworks ('depends') feel more expert than absolutes. The always-apology anchor keeps it human.
what_to_steal: The misuse → education rule for LC's support content: 'tarnishing' complaints that come from wearing non-waterproof pieces get an educational response (materials explainer), not a refund script — it turns complaints into content.

hook: "Most business owners are using AI to write captions. But AI can now help you create: Product videos…"
idea: AI video has moved past captions into product videos, promos, ads, brand stories, and educational content — the author is experimenting and will show more.
sequencing: Hook: everyone uses AI for captions.
The leap: product videos, promos, ads, stories, educational.
The note: experimenting with AI video.
formatting: AI-capability tease: the caption-only past → the 5-format future → the experiment note. 10s video.
why_it_works: 'Most are using AI for captions' makes the reader feel behind with a low bar — then the 5-format list shows how far behind.
what_to_steal: Educational content named among AI video's top uses — validates LC's AI-generated materials explainers as a core lane, not an experiment.

idea: A hiring signal: DTC health brands staff designers to turn campaigns, educational content, and promotions into strong visual concepts inside an established brand system.
sequencing: The work: statics, educational visuals, Figma system.
formatting: Job post: role, location, 4 bullet responsibilities. Hiring signal.
why_it_works: Public hiring posts reveal what serious brands invest in — educational content gets its own design pipeline.
what_to_steal: The role definition validates LC's need: a designer turning educational content into visual concepts inside LC's brand system — LC's educational lane needs dedicated design ownership.

hook: "There are a ton of your customers who know nothing about your brand. That's what educational ads are for."
body: The method: educational ads for customers who know nothing about the brand — the product doesn't appear until after the first 20 seconds. The 21s clip is spent on 'why dogs hide pain' (in the wild, a sick animal is a target) — pure education before any product. The product enters only once the viewer understands the problem.
cta: none explicit — the clip is the content (link cut).
idea: Educational ads withhold the product for the first 20+ seconds — spend the opening on the problem's 'why' (why dogs hide pain) so the product lands on educated attention.
sequencing: The premise: customers know nothing about you.
The job: that's what educational ads are for.
The rule: product appears only after this clip.
The example: 20s on why dogs hide pain.
formatting: Method reveal: the principle → the 20-second rule → the example clip. 21s video.
why_it_works: Withholding the product builds curiosity — the viewer stays to see what the education is FOR. 'Why dogs hide pain' proves education can be fascinating on its own.
what_to_steal: The 20-second product delay as LC's educational-ad rule: open LC's materials explainers with 'why your skin turns green' (the chemistry) — the LC piece appears only after the viewer understands the problem. Education-first is the TOF play.

hook: "There are a ton of your customers who know nothing about your brand."
idea: Same educational-ad method: product withheld for 20+ seconds while the opening teaches the problem's 'why.'
sequencing: The rule: product after the clip.
The example: why dogs hide pain.
formatting: Same method reveal, reshared: principle → 20-second rule → example. 21s video.
why_it_works: Repetition across two posters signals the method is a real internal playbook.
what_to_steal: Same steal: the 20-second delay rule for LC's educational ads.
